source: CARDI (2011), "Handbook of Integrated Techniques for Increasing Wet-Season and Dry-Season Rice Productivity" (Khmer, 50pp, funded by CAVAC/ACIAR, foreword by H.E. Chan Sarun, Minister of Agriculture, dated 26 August 2011)
text: Water management is described as the single most important input for wet-season rice, because different duration groups of rice tolerate different standing-water depths for different lengths of time. Light/non-photoperiod-sensitive, short-statured varieties (80–110 cm tall) tolerate standing water over 20 cm deep for up to 1 month; medium-duration, medium-height varieties (120–160 cm) tolerate over 30 cm for up to 1 month; heavy, tall varieties can tolerate standing water up to 50 cm deep for up to 1 month. For light/short-duration rice, keep standing water in the transplanted field no deeper than 5 cm, and hold that shallow depth for the first 20 days after transplanting; after that, drain the field for about 4–5 days if possible before re-flooding, to encourage vigorous root and tiller growth. For medium and heavy rice under 1 month old, likewise keep water no deeper than 5 cm; once the crop is past 1 month old, water depth can be allowed to rise up to 30 cm without hurting yield, since by then the taller/heavier types can tolerate it — and if possible, still drain the field for about 4–5 days around the active-tillering stage before re-flooding. Drain fields entirely about 20 days after the crop has finished flowering, keeping the soil surface moist and cracked but not muddy, and maintain that drained condition through to maturity — this typically falls in late October, which is usually when the wet season's rains are ending anyway for wet-season rice. Draining before harvest firms up the field for harvesting/threshing and helps the crop mature and dry down evenly.
